MoSPI’s next quarterly GDP release, covering Q2 FY 2026-27, is scheduled for November 30, 2026.

title: Canada expands EDC trade support for exporters
summary:
Export Development Canada will expand its Trade Impact Program from September 1, 2026, widening financing, insurance and risk-management support for tariff-hit exporters.
EDC will assume more risk through a $700 million financing envelope within up to $5 billion in added capacity.
Smaller exporters can use guarantees, credit insurance and foreign-exchange tools to protect access and diversify.

title: India pushes TRAs towards industry-led, outcome-driven textile R&D
summary:
Ministry of Textiles held the second TRA coordination meet to make India’s textile R&D more industry-led, collaborative and outcome-based.
Discussions covered technical textiles, Centres of Excellence, New Age Fibres, startups, funding, skills, governance and i-TRAMS mapping.
TRA plans for 2026–27 will target testing, standardisation, commercialisation, import substitution and MSME solutions.

title: Afghanistan, Uzbekistan traders sign $267mn trade agreements
summary:
Afghan and Uzbek traders sealed 20 agreements worth $267 million in Kabul recently.
The accords cover foodstuffs, textiles and apparel, construction materials, livestock, consumer electronics and furniture.
For manufacturers and sourcing teams, the deal signals wider cross-border commercial activity.
Earlier 2026 memorandums were valued at over $1 billion.

title: Indonesia building wastewater treatment plant for SMEs in Kalimantan
summary:
Indonesia is constructing a wastewater treatment plant in Tapin Regency using green technology for SMEs in south Kalimantan. 
The facility, being built under the Industrial Technology Enhancement Partnership Fund programme, will allow traditional Sasirangan textile SMEs to reuse around 90 per cent of treated wastewater, boosting operational efficiency while maintaining environmental sustainability.

title: DTY nylon 6 firms: How far will feedstock costs push it?
summary:
Chinese nylon 6 DTY filament yarn prices moved modestly higher from August 26 to 28, 2026, as crude-linked feedstock costs rose.
Naphtha gained about 3.7 per cent and benzene about 2.5 per cent, ahead of caprolactam's 0.61 per cent rise and nylon 6 chips' 0.80 per cent increase.
DTY pass-through was uneven: 40D/36F rose 0.76 per cent, 70D/24F 0.33 per cent and 50D/24F stayed flat.

title: FDY rises as Brent falls 5%, could the cost shock extend in September?
summary:

TexPro tracked FDY 100D/72F up 1.09 per cent to CNY 9,250 per mt, while FDY 75D/36F rose 0.53 per cent to CNY 9,500 per mt.
FDY 150D/96F gained 0.33 per cent to CNY 9.175 per kg, with early-week increases holding through the weekend.

summary:

India’s Shankar-6 traded flat at INR 199 per kg, supported by comfortable surplus supplies.
China’s 3128B fell to CNY 18,527.28 per tonne on Thursday, rebounded 0.53 per cent on Friday and rose 0.82 per cent on August 31.

summary:
Uzbekistan and Chinese textile firms plan deeper cooperation in raw materials, technology, investment and joint production.
China’s cotton-complex imports from Uzbekistan reached about $154.5 million in January–June 2026, up roughly 329 per cent.
Cotton yarn drove almost the entire increase, rising 339 per cent to $154.5 million, while small fabric flows fell to zero.

summary:

The benchmark recovered 41 cents to 1,853 cents, as the pass-in rate fell to around 2 per cent on 23,651 bales offered.
The move signals a brief mechanical reset, not weakening demand, with tight supply limiting wool input cost relief.

title: Tk 30,000 wage demand could raise Bangladesh’s SS27 risk
summary:
Bangladesh’s garment sector is entering its first minimum-wage review under a shortened three-year cycle, with unions seeking reconstitution of the Minimum Wage Board. 
The last structure took effect in December 2023, pointing to a new one by December 2026 under the amended labour law. 
RMG exports were US$39.35 billion in FY2024-25, up 8.84 per cent, with an 81.49 per cent share of total exports.

title: 26-point duty gap could favour flexible apparel sourcing
summary:
A rebuilt United States tariff structure is shifting apparel sourcing from choosing one country to moving between several quickly. 
India’s PDS Limited and Indonesia’s Busana Apparel Group have announced a non-binding alliance across six manufacturing locations. 
New Section 301 duties create a landed-cost gap that could favour CAFTA-DR apparel from Honduras and Nicaragua.

title: Can solar energy ease Bangladesh RMG sector’s power woes?
summary:
Bangladesh garment factories could generate up to 1,768 MWp of rooftop solar using nearly 9.7 million square metres of roof space. 
It could meet around 40 per cent of large factories’ power demand, 38 per cent for small units and 33 per cent for medium units. 
Upfront costs, financing and technical barriers remain; BGMEA-Bidec fan trials saved 47 per cent to nearly 65 per cent electricity.

summary:
Bangladesh’s RMG exports rose by 11 per cent YoY to $10.10 billion during Q4 FY26, the Bangladesh Bank’s quarterly review of the sector said.

The near-term outlook for the sector is moderately positive.

China’s shipments rose 12.90 per cent to $52.159 million, lifting its share to 56.25 per cent.
India stayed second at $17.053 million, just $512,000 ahead of Bangladesh.
China, India and Bangladesh accounted for 92.48 per cent of imports.

title: Evolving Middle East crisis raising fresh risks for Indian exporters?
summary:
Iran-US tensions and Houthi attacks in the Red Sea are adding risks around the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb for Indian businesses.

Readymade garment exporters to Europe may see pressure on prices, margins, delivery commitments and supply-chain certainty.
